body.statement: The map \(\operatorname{OR}:(0,1)^2\to(0,\infty)\) has no path-independent continuous extension at \((0,0)\) or \((1,1)\), so \(\theta_{a,x}\) is used only on the strictly positive chart \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  For each \(r\in(0,1)\) and finite \(\theta>0\), \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\), \(q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\), and the endpoint objectives \(H_x^-\) and \(H_x^+\) extend continuously in \((w_0,w_1)\) to all of the compact region \(D_{A,x}\), including the constant-\(U\) corners.
body.justification: This separates the interior odds-ratio chart from the compact probability-scale optimization that attains boundary endpoints.
body.gap: Fixed-parameter binary-confounder calculations do not distinguish the odds-ratio chart from its well-defined probability-scale boundary objectives.
body.consumer: The sharpness theorem and exact verifier can include null latent cells without assigning an ill-defined boundary odds ratio.
body.proof_tex:
For any fixed \(c>0\), as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\),
\[
\operatorname{OR}(c\varepsilon,\varepsilon)
=\frac{c(1-\varepsilon)}{1-c\varepsilon}\longrightarrow c.
\]
Distinct values of \(c\) give distinct limits at \((0,0)\).  Likewise,
\[
\operatorname{OR}(1-c\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)
=\frac{1-c\varepsilon}{c(1-\varepsilon)}\longrightarrow c^{-1},
\]
so no path-independent continuous extension exists at \((1,1)\).  Hence the odds-ratio coordinate \(\theta_{a,x}\) is properly confined to \(\mathcal M^\circ\).

For fixed \(r\in(0,1)\) and finite \(\theta>0\), the proof of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) represents \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\) as the unique inverse of the continuous, strictly increasing map \(f_\theta\).  Its displayed radical formula has positive denominator also at \(w=0,1\), and therefore is continuous in \(w\in[0,1]\); the value at \(\theta=1\) is its removable limit \(r\).  It follows from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}adjusted\text{-}arm\text{-}mean}\) that \(q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\) is continuous on \([0,1]^2\), because \(\pi_x=p_xw_1+(1-p_x)w_0\) is affine and every displayed denominator is positive.

The region \(D_{A,x}\) is the intersection of \([0,1]^2\) with two inverse images of \(({-}\infty,0]\) under polynomials, hence it is closed and compact.  A minimum or maximum of two continuous functions is continuous, since
\[
\min(f,g)=\frac{f+g-|f-g|}{2},
\qquad
\max(f,g)=\frac{f+g+|f-g|}{2}.
\]
Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}endpoints}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) now imply that \(q^-_{a,x}\), \(q^+_{a,x}\), \(H_x^-\), and \(H_x^+\) extend continuously to all of \(D_{A,x}\).  At a constant-confounder corner \((w_0,w_1)=(c,c)\), with \(c\in\{0,1\}\), one has \(\pi_x=w_{a,x}=c\), so the identity
\[
q_{a,x}-r_{a,x}=(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(m_1-m_0)
\]
gives \(q_{a,x}=r_{a,x}\) for every finite \(\theta\).  Thus the compact probability-scale objective is well defined at precisely the corners where the odds-ratio chart itself is not.
